title: Challenge: mount a Secret as env vars and as files
intro: Give an app a secret two ways, as an environment variable and as a mounted file, exactly like this post. Commands are checked; the output is illustrative, so no real cluster is needed.

steps.instruction: Create a generic Secret named 'supersecret' in the 'example' namespace, with MY_SUPER_ENVVAR=a_secret.
steps.hint: kubectl create secret generic supersecret -n example --from-literal=MY_SUPER_ENVVAR=a_secret

steps.instruction: Inspect the secret as YAML to see how Kubernetes stored it (base64-encoded).
steps.success:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: supersecret
data:
  MY_SUPER_ENVVAR: YV9zZWNyZXQ=   # base64 of 'a_secret'
type: Opaque
steps.hint: kubectl get secret supersecret -n example -o yaml

steps.instruction: Apply the Deployment that injects the secret as the env var MY_SUPER_ENVVAR (via secretKeyRef).
steps.fail: Apply the deployment manifest with kubectl apply -f <file>.

steps.instruction: Verify the env var made it inside the pod: exec into the pod and print its environment, filtering for ENV.
steps.success:
MY_SUPER_ENVVAR=a_secret
ANOTHER_ENVVAR=just_another_secret   <- the secret is now an env var in the container
steps.fail: kubectl exec into the pod and print its env (e.g. piped to grep ENV).
steps.hint: kubectl -n example exec -ti <pod> -- env | grep ENV

steps.instruction: Now the file way: apply the Deployment that mounts the secret as files under /var/mysecrets.
Read the mounted secret file inside the pod, under /var/mysecrets.
steps.success: {"db":"prod","password":"s3cr3t"}   <- same secret, now a file at /var/mysecrets/test.json (each key becomes a file)
steps.fail: kubectl exec into the pod and cat the file under /var/mysecrets.

done: Solved! One Secret, two consumption styles: env vars (secretKeyRef) and mounted files (volume + volumeMounts). File mounts are usually safer, they don't show up in the process environment or in `kubectl describe pod`.
